title: Today / Morning Brief
markdown:
**What it is:** A single screen of *what needs you right now* — the proactive digest the Executive prepares so you're not the one chasing status. In the app it's **Home**, the screen the app opens on.

**What it does:**

- Opens with a greeting, one line summing up the day (click a part of it — *2 awaiting reply*, *1 department at risk* — to open that list), and an **Ask your Executive anything…** box that starts a chat.
- Puts what's waiting on your call up front under **Needs you**: the first card large, the next two below it, and **Show N more** for the rest.
- Gathers everything else under **Everything else** as a row of count tiles — **Departments**, **People**, **Across the team** (waiting on someone else), **In flight**, **Handled overnight**, **Monitoring** — shown only when they have something in them. Click a tile to open its full list in a side panel.
- The **Departments** tile shows each department's goal health — on-track, at-risk, or off-track — with the at-risk goals called out.
- The **People** tile lists people with open items, their reply counts, SLA status, and whether they're on leave.
- **Read today's brief** (next to **Needs you**) opens the written brief — what's going on across the company — in a side panel.
- If your latest morning brief, end-of-day digest or weekly review couldn't be sent to you, a line at the top says why and what to connect. It goes away once that's fixed.
- With **Settings → Act as me → Draft replies to my inbox** on, the replies the Executive wrote in your Gmail Drafts for mail that needs you come first in **Needs you**. Only you see them.
- Surfaces proposals and alerts you can click to open a chat thread with full context.

**How to use:**

1. Click **Home** in the sidebar (or the Open Executive logo). On a phone, **Home** is the first button in the bar at the bottom.
2. Work **Needs you** from the top. Each card has one main button and **Discuss**; everything else is in the card's **⋯** menu:
   - **Approve** — accept the recommendation; a chat opens so the Executive can carry it out. Usually the main button.
   - **Discuss** — open a chat with the context already filled in.
   - **Edit & approve** (in **⋯**) — reword the action first, then **Send approval**; your text is used exactly as written.
   - **Dismiss** (in **⋯**) — drop it and stay on Home. When the Executive thinks a card is stale, **Dismiss** is the main button instead.
   - **Nudge *name*** — the main button when the best move is chasing someone for a reply; **Run *workflow*** when the best move is a workflow.
   - **Open *name*'s page** (in **⋯**) — the person the item is waiting on.
3. Some cards are simpler: a document card's main button is **Open document** (**Mark reviewed** is in its **⋯**), and a calendar-booking card books (or declines) the meeting directly when you click Approve or Dismiss. Only the person a booking was sent to for approval, or the owner, can approve or decline it.
4. Keep it tidy from the **⋯** next to **Needs you**: **Dismiss N older than 7 days** clears stale items, and **Re-check relevance** asks the Executive to review every open item now.
5. Open the **Departments** tile and click a department to ask for its status in chat.
6. Work the replies waiting to be sent (they come first in **Needs you**): each card shows who wrote (and whether Gmail could confirm their address), what they wrote, your draft, and **Decide before sending** — what the draft leaves for you to answer. **Send** asks you once, naming who the reply goes to, then sends the draft from your Gmail exactly as it is there. If you changed who it goes to in Gmail, or they wrote again since, it asks a second time and says what changed. To change the wording, choose **Edit in Gmail** in the card's **⋯**, edit the draft there, then Send here or from Gmail. **Dismiss** (also in **⋯**) deletes the draft, unless you've already edited it in Gmail. On a server, Send needs signed sign-ins; until they're set up, send from Gmail. A card goes away on its own once you send or delete the draft in Gmail, or reply yourself, and after a week.

**Example:** in a Discuss thread, just say *"go ahead"* to approve the proposal or *"drop it"* to dismiss it — no need to go back to the card. (Calendar bookings still need the Approve button.)

**Just for yourself?** If you use Open Executive just for yourself (**Settings → Workspace → Personal**), Home leaves out the team parts: there are no Departments, People or Across the team tiles — everything that needs a decision is in **Needs you**. When a goal is slipping, the summary line at the top says how many goals are at risk; click it to open **Goals**. Instead, the tiles are **Due soon**, **Your projects** and **This week's review**, each opening its list in a side panel. **Your projects** lists the projects the Executive is tracking for you. Click **Done** when one is finished, or **Drop** to stop tracking it (it asks first, and removes the project from Pulse). **Due soon** lists what you've promised by a date and what others have asked of you, due in the next week — say *"I'll send Northwind the proposal by Friday"* in the web chat or your own Slack or Discord and it shows up here, and the Executive reminds you when it's due. Click **Done** once it's handled; **All open items** opens the full list. **Top three today**, right under **Needs you**, shows the three things to focus on today — the same three your morning brief opens with — each with a free slot in today's working hours when the Executive can read your calendar. **This week's review** shows your latest weekly review: when it ran and next week's top three. Click **Read the review** to see all of it.

Your morning brief also opens with a **top three for today**, picked from what's overdue or due, goals that are slipping and the projects you're driving. When Google Workspace is connected and the Executive can read your calendar (it is your own account, or you shared your calendar with it), each of the three gets a free slot in today's working hours and the brief lists today's meetings; otherwise the three come without times. Every Friday afternoon (in your time zone) a **weekly review** arrives the same way: your goals graded by area, what's due or overdue, projects that went quiet, the week's decisions, a few older decisions to look back on, and next week's top three. Both also show up on Home (see above), so you see them even when no chat app or email is connected. When it asks how an older decision turned out, just tell the Executive in the web chat or your own Slack or Discord and it records the outcome against that decision.

*Note: proposals are routed to the right person automatically based on who has authority over them.*
